guarantees.claim: wr_err is asserted (1) if reg_we is high and any addr_hit[i] is high and the bitwise reduction OR of (HMAC_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be) is non-zero; otherwise wr_err is 0.

assumptions.claim: HMAC_PERMIT[i] correctly encodes the set of byte lanes that are legal to write for the register decoded at addr_hit[i]; any mismatch (too permissive or too restrictive) will cause wr_err to misflag.
assumptions.risk: Legal writes may be blocked (if too restrictive) or illegal partial writes may go undetected (if too permissive), leading to register corruption.

assumptions.claim: addr_hit is a one-hot decoded signal; at most one bit is set at any time.
assumptions.risk: If multiple addr_hit bits are high simultaneously, a write error could be spuriously asserted even if the targeted register’s byte enable matches its permit, confusing software error handling.

uncertain_points.claim: The values of HMAC_PERMIT array (indexed 0..58) are defined elsewhere; they must enforce that secret/key registers (e.g., KEY, config) are only writable with specific byte-enable masks (likely full-word only). If any HMAC_PERMIT[i] is too permissive, an attacker could partially overwrite key material.
uncertain_points.cond: when a write targets a security-sensitive register (e.g., KEY)
uncertain_points.risk: Partial overwrite of HMAC key register, leading to key extraction or integrity failure; or silent bypass of write-protection.

security_implications: wr_err is the write-error detector for the HMAC register interface. If HMAC_PERMIT masks for key registers are not set to require full-word writes, or if the logic fails to assert wr_err on mismatched byte enables, an attacker could partially overwrite HMAC key material (e.g., overwriting only one byte of the key) and potentially infer the key or bypass authentication. This chunk must be verified to correctly flag any partial write to security-critical registers.
